rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Round End 4 Game End Overview Be the Youngest at game end Turn Play a card in a number of ways You can play a number card on an opponent adjacent to you if the number is one higher than either number they have, e.g. if they are 37 you can either play a 4 or an 8 for 47 or 38 respectively You can play a special card (including 0) to trigger some effect If you can't do either of the above, you have to make yourself older but this increase can be by as much as you wish (it isn't limited by a single value like against opponents) In this way, you can choose to play a card facedown and consider it a 9 If you have no possible play, skip your turn until end of round After you end your go, draw back up to 4 cards (Note, you may start your turn with less than 4 cards if you played a special on someone else's turn) Round End There are two round end triggers If the deck runs out, round ends If you exceed 90, at the start of each turn reveal a card from the deck, if this number added to your age is greater than 99 then the round ends However the round ended, log each player's age as their current score Game End At the end of the third round, the youngest player wins!

[Rating: 2/10] A different type of Uno...it's fine for a relatively quick game with a younger crowd or light situation but it can be incredibly frustrating to see everyone else get the special cards and you keep drawing lousy number cards that force you to up your age instead.   Probably better at higher player counts...and it may be better to bump up your 10's instead of your 1's at times...you can quickly get yourself in trouble and have to jump to a 9 in the 10's column when you get burned by your card draw...

[Rating: 2/10] Maybe I'm missing something here, but this game doesn't feel enjoyable to me at all. You regularly don't have actual decisions to make and are limited by the luck of the draw. And you can be limited even more if your opponents are the ones drawing the special cards while you don't. Even when you do draw special cards, they are, at best, uninteresting take-that types of abilities to really set your opponent back. [Rating: 4/10] Your goal is to not get to an age of 100. Start with two cards that give you a two digit age and then play a card to increase your age or an opponent's age on your left or right by 1. There are also some action cards that can change things around too. Overall the game is just too random for me as there is just too little control. In a way it feels like a spin on Uno with all of the take that or being stuck having to age yourself up instead of one of your opponents. Definitely a pass for me.
